subject: business-studies
title: Break-even Adventure
welcome_lead: Where do you stop losing money and start winning? Find the break-even point. ⚖️
meta_desc: Finance & Profit Adventure 2 — KS3 Business Studies on break-even and contribution.
final_note: You learned what break-even means and how to find it using simple numbers.

concepts.def: What customers pay for one item
How many items are made or sold
How much extra you sell above break-even
The profit a business aims for

walkthroughs.body_html:
Break-even is the point where revenue = total costs.

Below it = loss. Above it = profit. Right at it = no profit, no loss. 🎯

Contribution = selling price − variable cost per item.

Cookies sell at £2, ingredients cost £0.50. Contribution = £1.50.

Each cookie pays £1.50 toward the rent.

Break-even output = fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit.

Fixed costs £300, contribution £1.50 each → break-even = 200 cookies.

Sell 250 → margin of safety is 50 cookies. 🛡️

numericals.q: Fixed cost £400, contribution £2 each. Break-even units?
